name: Chiloé
tagline: Stilt houses, wooden churches and island myths
summary: Chiloé is a misty, green island in southern Chile with its own culture and myths. See the colourful palafitos stilt houses of Castro, visit some of its 16 UNESCO wooden churches, watch Humboldt and Magellanic penguins at Puñihuil, and eat curanto, a feast cooked in an earth pit.
seasonNote: Summer is mildest; rain is likely any time.
arrival: Ferry from Pargua near Puerto Montt (30 minutes), then buses; flights to Castro.
gettingAround: Buses between towns; a car is easiest.
cashTip: Carry pesos; cards work in Castro and Ancud. Tip 10 percent.
foodTip: Curanto, milcao potato bread, and seafood from the islands.

connections.note: Flights to Castro or Puerto Montt.
Via Puerto Montt and the ferry.
